title: Path Traversal and Arbitrary File Creation/Deletion in CLI
description: The command-line interface constructs database and report paths directly using the videoId parameter without sanitizing path traversal characters (such as ../). An attacker who controls the input parameters can overwrite or delete files outside the intended directories.
evidence: const dbPath = `./temp_${VIDEO_ID}.sqlite`; and later unlinkSync(dbPath) on cleanup, as well as mdPath, csvPath, and cleanCsvPath construction.
impact: Arbitrary file creation and deletion in the context of the running process, potentially leading to local file overwriting, data loss, or configuration corruption.
remediation: Sanitize the videoId input using a strict regular expression validation (e.g., matching the standard YouTube 11-character alphanumeric/symbolic format /^[a-zA-Z0-9_-]{11}$/) before building any path.

title: Overly Permissive CORS Origin Subdomain Validation
description: The Cloudflare Worker CORS check allows cross-origin requests from any Origin ending in .pages.dev. Because anyone can deploy websites on pages.dev, this allows unauthorized applications to communicate directly with the worker.
impact: Exhaustion of backend server API quotas, data exposure, and unauthorized proxy request routing on behalf of untrusted origins.
remediation: Restrict the CORS ends-with check to the specific pages.dev subdomains belonging to the organization (e.g. '.rasalytics.pages.dev') or require strict, literal Origin matches.

title: Missing Content-Security-Policy (CSP)
description: The static web frontend does not configure a Content-Security-Policy (CSP) meta tag or headers, leaving the application open to DOM-based XSS attacks and frame hijacking (clickjacking).
evidence: No CSP meta tags found in the head of index.html, and no deploy-time header configurations exist.
impact: Enhanced likelihood of successful DOM-based XSS execution and embedding of the app into clickjacking frames if input sanitization is bypassed.
remediation: Introduce a meta CSP tag in index.html (or deploy a _headers file for Cloudflare Pages) restricting default-src, script-src, and frame-ancestors.

title: Missing Subresource Integrity (SRI) on External CDN Scripts
description: The web application imports external libraries (Chart.js and WordCloud2) from third-party CDN domains without specifying a cryptographic integrity hash. If the CDN domain is compromised, the client script execution is poisoned.
impact: Remote code execution (RCE) in client browsers via supply chain compromise of the external CDNs.
remediation: Add appropriate integrity hashes and crossorigin='anonymous' properties to external script imports, or compile/bundle dependencies locally.

title: Exposure of PII in Data Samples
location: data/samples/Presiden Prabowo Bertolak ke Lampung dalam Rangka Kunjungan Kerja, 10 Juni 2026 [-2gsJ0uXQqo].info.json:1
description: The repository includes sample files containing real YouTube usernames, channel IDs, user URLs, avatar thumbnails, and raw comments. Storing actual user identities violates privacy engineering practices.
evidence: Presence of comments array in the info.json with values such as 'author': '@pejuangcinta5103' and 'author_id': 'UCuSf32hPRVUkuZgjGMGpFBg'.
impact: Accidental exposure of end-user profiles in public source control, resulting in compliance or privacy check failures.
remediation: Redact or mock all usernames, channel IDs, and URLs in data/samples/ and data/fixtures/ before committing them.

title: Prompt Injection Vulnerability in AI-Agent Skills
description: AI agent skill descriptions and yaml configurations instruct models to run comment sentiment analyses and exports without prompt constraints. An agent processing a comment containing prompt injection (e.g. 'Ignore other guidelines...') could execute unintended tools.
evidence: Lack of instructions in SKILL.md files and agents/openai.yaml guiding agents to treat comments purely as untrusted data parameters.
impact: Manipulation of agent actions, incorrect reports, or unauthorized tool executions if the LLM processes malicious comment text directly.
remediation: Add prompt insulation guidelines in the SKILL.md files, instructing agents to sandbox comment content and block instruction evaluation from raw comment variables.

title: Unpinned (Mutable Tag) Third-Party GitHub Actions
description: GitHub Action workflows use mutable tag versions (such as @v4 and @v2) instead of specific, immutable Git commit SHA hashes, exposing the pipeline to tag hijacking.
evidence: uses: actions/checkout@v4, uses: gitleaks/gitleaks-action@v2, and uses: oven-sh/setup-bun@v1 in compliance.yml and test.yml.
impact: Supply chain compromise of CI/CD pipeline leading to malicious code execution in the build environment.
remediation: Pin all third-party workflows to their full 40-character commit SHA, using tools like Renovate or Dependabot to maintain updates securely.

title: Overly Permissive Default GITHUB_TOKEN permissions
description: The CI/CD workflow files compliance.yml and test.yml do not restrict default permissions for the GITHUB_TOKEN, letting the jobs inherit default write scopes.
evidence: Absence of a top-level permissions block in both workflow files.
impact: A compromised runner or script could leverage permissions to modify repository contents, releases, or pull requests.
remediation: Add an explicit permissions: read-all or permissions: contents: read block to all workflow definitions.

title: Error Message and Quota Information Leakage
description: The Cloudflare Worker forwards raw YouTube API error bodies directly to clients and leaks internal error messages on general catch blocks.
evidence: return new Response(JSON.stringify({ error: "YouTube API Error: " + errText }) and err.message propagation on catch blocks.
impact: Exposing system limits, internal API payloads, and endpoint status details to potential attackers.
remediation: Log detailed API issues internally and return simplified, generic messages (e.g. 'Failed to fetch comment threads') to clients.

title: Over-broad Caret (^) Dependency Version Constraints
description: Dependencies in all package.json files are configured with caret (^) ranges, allowing arbitrary minor/patch updates during install and increasing dependency hijack risks.
evidence: Caret prefixes in dependencies block, e.g. '@xenova/transformers': '^2.17.2', 'zod': '^4.4.3', etc.
impact: Accidental installation of breaking package changes or compromised patches during deployment.
remediation: Pin exact dependency versions in package.json files and enforce locks with strict SHA verification in bun.lock.

title: Risky trustedDependencies Configuration
description: Root package.json authorizes Bun to execute postinstall scripts automatically for sharp and protobufjs. If these upstream libraries are hijacked, postinstall execution acts as a vector.
impact: Malicious code execution on developer machines or CI build runners during dependency install.
remediation: Verify need for postinstall lifecycle hooks, or audit package hashes before installations.

title: Broken Skill Symbolic Link
description: The configuration folder contains a broken symlink pointing to a missing skill folder under .agents/skills/.
evidence: The symlink .claude/skills/youtube-comments-scraper points to missing target ../../.agents/skills/youtube-comments-scraper.
impact: Broken references in the directory tree which could disrupt file scanning tools or local configurations.
remediation: Remove the broken symlink or create the target directory under .agents/skills/.
